actions: Compared public 2026 continual-LLM adaptation evidence for shared subspaces, task-specific blocks, and routed mixtures.
Pinned public repository heads for SLoRA and Share.
Separated strict Share from Share-full and identified task-specific coefficient persistence as a scope constraint.
Separated SLoRA's routing-free inference/storage story from its train-time task-boundary dependence.
Corrected MoBLoRA interpretation: shared bases retain task-specific mixing matrices and semantic routing.
Persisted a new role-local checkpoint and advanced the role-local latest pointer.
material_update: The shared-vs-routed design question is now decomposed into persistent storage, task-specific growth, inference selection, and train-time boundary assumptions. SLoRA provides a strong non-routed but boundary-aware LLM control; strict Share is far more parameter-efficient but weaker than its relaxed Share-full result and retains task-specific coefficients; ASO-LoRA avoids inference routing via growing merged task blocks; MoBLoRA still semantically routes task-specific mixing matrices.
termination: physical invocation boundary only; recurring research frontier remains active
exact_next_action: Inspect Share strict inference coefficient selection and SLoRA adapter lifecycle, then build a matched-budget matrix across SLoRA/Share/ASO-LoRA/MoBLoRA/PASs-MoE and seek a genuinely boundary-free continual-language comparison. Preserve CLDD and DRIFT continuation items.
